description: A single-panel schematic load–displacement curve of an indentation test, drawn with two smooth solid curves on a plain white background. The vertical axis is labelled "Load   P" with an upward arrowhead; the horizontal axis is labelled "Indentation depth   h" with a rightward arrowhead. Neither axis carries numeric ticks or gridlines, so the plot is qualitative and no magnitudes are printed. The first solid curve, annotated "load", rises from the origin with a concave-up shape to the peak point. The second solid curve, annotated "unload", descends from that same peak back towards the depth axis, its lower portion overlaid by a straight dashed tangent line whose slope is labelled with the equation S = dP/dh. A horizontal dashed line marks the peak load and is labelled "Pmax"; a vertical dashed line drops from the peak to the depth axis. The unloading branch is not perfectly smooth — it shows a slight hook or kink partway down. The figure defines the standard Oliver–Pharr indentation quantities: maximum load Pmax, maximum indentation depth, and contact stiffness S taken as the initial slope of the unloading curve.

subfigures.description: Schematic indentation load–displacement curve: solid loading branch labelled "load" and solid unloading branch labelled "unload"; horizontal dashed line labelled "Pmax" at the peak and vertical dashed line from peak to the depth axis; straight dashed tangent on the unloading branch labelled "S = dP/dh". Axes are "Load P" and "Indentation depth h" with no numeric ticks.

observations.observation: The plot axes are labelled "Load   P" (vertical) and "Indentation depth   h" (horizontal), both drawn as arrows, and carry no numeric tick marks or gridlines.
Two solid curves are drawn and annotated in the image: an ascending curve labelled "load" and a descending curve labelled "unload".
A horizontal dashed line at the curve maximum is labelled "Pmax".
A straight dashed tangent line is drawn along the lower part of the unloading curve and labelled with the expression S = dP/dh, i.e. contact stiffness defined as the slope of the unloading curve.
The unloading branch shows a small hook/kink partway down rather than being perfectly smooth; whether this is a real feature or a drawing artefact cannot be determined from the image alone.
The loading and unloading curves meet at a single peak point, from which a vertical dashed line drops to the indentation-depth axis.
The caption states the figure is a "Typical load and displacement curve of indentation".
The citing text states that Fig. 6 shows a typical load–displacement curve and the indentation trace; the image confirms the load–displacement curve but contains no separate indentation-trace panel.

The citing text describes the apparatus as a 3D piezo stage driven by a transducer controller, with AFM-mode scanning of the sample surface before and after indentation so that the indentation point can be chosen to nanometre order and the profile measured in situ.
